title: Matrix powers and polynomial identities

question.text:
A real 2 × 2 matrix satisfies (A − I)(A − 2I) = 0. Which statement must hold?
(A) A = I
(B) A = 2I
(C) A − I is invertible
2
(D) (2I − A) = 2I − A
(E) A has two equal diagonal entries

solution.text:
2 2 2
Expand the given identity as A − 3A + 2I = 0. Then (2I − A) = 4I − 4A + A =
2I − A. The matrix diag(1, 2) disproves the other four claims. A zero product need not make
either factor zero.

This is a terminating geometric-series identity.
